entities.summary:
Claude-Louis de La Châtre (1745-09-30, Paris – 1824-07-13) was a French military commander, diplomat, and politician of the 18th and 19th centuries. As a prominent figure in the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars, he played a crucial role in the Grande Armée's military campaigns in Europe.

 He held various positions, including Minister of War, Ambassador to Russia, and Prefect of the Seine. His diplomatic efforts helped secure the Treaty of Amiens (1802) and the Treaty of Tilsit (1807), which marked significant turning points in European history. La Châtre's military prowess and strategic thinking earned him recognition as a capable commander, but his involvement in the wars also left him with personal and financial scars.

 His legacy extends beyond his own era, with his experiences and decisions influencing the development of modern European politics and military strategy. Despite his significant contributions, La Châtre's life and career remain relatively overshadowed by those of his contemporaries, reflecting the complexities of historical memory and the challenges of evaluating the impact of individual actors in shaping the course of world events.
